Clean Data Architecture · Field notes

Federation is an organisational principle, not an execution model

How product thinking, platform engineering and organisational design turn governance into executable capabilities.

Gaëlle Seret & Axel Mercier · Data Mesh Belgium · 2026

Speakers

Who's speaking today

Gaëlle Seret

Head of Data Governance

Works for leboncoin as Head of Data Governance.

Axel Mercier

Head of Data Platform

Works for Kering as Head of Data Platform.

01 — Context

Federation has become one of the standards

Example of a pragmatic data strategy:

Data for all

Fast access to information. Capacity to do agentic.

Data by all

Clear, distributed responsibility.

99.9%of people we work with agree that it is a good idea
02 — Problem

Why is federated governance not adopted?

Because it adds problems to people who already have enough.

We need to bring something to the table.

Governance must solve user problems and start with discovery.

03 — Discovery

Problem discovery and prioritization

Mapping your users into personas, knowing their pain points and expectations in detail

Where can you deliver the most value and create future allyship?

Executive Committee

For the value I have invested in governance, are we doing better or worse?

Privacy teams

Where are our risks, and how can we update this map regularly?

Architecture teams

How do we design the organisation as one team?

Chief Data Officer

How do we kill the legacy?

04 — Focusing on killing the legacy

A key foundation for future federation

First, we map existing data assets to functional domains.

Then, we create functional domains not as teams but as sets of nodes that make sense together: multiple teams that functionally need to work together.

05 — Computational by design

Computational supports Domain-Driven Design

Every node is a data asset, owned by a domain.
Every asset is built and exposed as a product.
Every link is a partnership, on the terms the asset publishes.

Data outlives the organisation. It is always accessible, with an owner accountable for what it exposes.

06 — Supporting teams in the process

Computational makes compliance a feature

Governance is here to reduce risks, not block delivery, or even worse innovation.

The platform blocks only what breaks production and computes everything else as a signal.

To do that, everything is designed within teams' ways of working, from creation to deprecation.

1

Service · Enable

Compliant by construction.
One common access process.

2

CI · Block

Only what breaks production.
Contracts, breaking changes, builds.

3

Monitoring · Guide

Signals, not stop signs.
Open PRs, budgets, quotas.

4

Reporting · Arbitrate

Contested rules go to council.
Policies nobody values.

07 — Enabling policy as code

The benefits of policy as code for each user

1

Product

What is a quality data product?

2

Engineering

What is the technical debt and how mature are the teams?

3

Chief Data Officer

Can we monitor costs and compliance with security standards?

08 — It shows that we need federation

Policies alone are not enough

Delivering policies shows that federation is now necessary. The teams who comply are rarely the ones who suffer from the problem the policies address.

Computation makes every problem visible and its impact understood.

Remediation requires federation.

Example · Policy

dbt tests on every data product

28%still do not comply

Complying is costly, and many producers sit outside the organisation.

Our path: data product health → quality framework → dbt tests.

09 — Working to incentivise teams

Going back to our 4 personas

The computational design solves problems for the users and for the teams participating in the mesh.

Engineering and Product teams have a strong incentive to participate in federation, even though we don't directly address their problems.

1

Reporting by design

2

Privacy by design

3

Architecture by design

4

Opening

Opening on what we are still exploring today

How to adapt policies and guidelines with AI.

10 — What about AI?

Governance usually gives guardrails to humans. Now the guardrails go to agents

Before

Service makes compliance a feature.
CI and monitoring block and guide.
Reporting arbitrates.

Now

Policies become platform documentation.
Practices write skills, governance curates.
Agents use them as skills and context.

Goodhart trap

An agent will cover a policy without thinking. A proxy rule like "at least one test" gets satisfied, not served. Policies have to be adapted for agents.

Conclusion

In the end, it's product

1

A product

Governance is a product that serves users.

2

Delivery

To be adopted, governance needs to serve the delivery process.

3

Strategy and debt

Governance is there to drive the product strategy and the technical debt.
